relations.definition: to declare or make known officially
relations.embedding_query_text: announces: to declare or make known officially

chosen_property.label: announces
chosen_property.definition: to declare or make known officially
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation phrase 'announces'.

candidates.label: announcementLocation
candidates.comment: An announcement location relation between a special announcement and the specific civic structure or local business it pertains to. Also called relevant location, associated place, specific venue. Examples: "A special announcement's announcement location is 'City Hall'.", "The emergency announcement's announcement location is 'Local Grocery Store'." Distinct from spatialCoverage, which is used for larger geographic regions.

candidates.label: recognizingAuthority
candidates.comment: A recognizing authority relation between a medical entity and the organization that officially endorses it within a system of medicine. Also called endorsed by, officially recognized by. Examples: "A medical treatment is recognized by 'the World Health Organization'.", "A medical specialty is recognized by 'the American Medical Association'.", "A traditional medicine practice is recognized by 'a national health ministry'."

candidates.label: releaseDate
candidates.comment: A release date relation between a product and the date it was made available to the public. Also called launch date, availability date, publication date. Examples: "A new smartphone model has a release date of 2024-03-01.", "A software update has a release date of 2023-11-15.", "A new car model has a release date of 2025-01-01.". Distinct from productionDate, which is when the item was manufactured.

candidates.label: quarantineGuidelines
candidates.comment: A quarantine guidelines relation between a special announcement and information regarding quarantine rules. Also called isolation rules, self-quarantine instructions. Examples: "A special announcement provides quarantine guidelines for travelers.", "A public health update includes quarantine guidelines for close contacts.", "A government notice details quarantine guidelines for returning citizens."

candidates.label: releasedEvent
candidates.comment: A released event relation between a creative work and the publication event marking its release. Also called release event, launch event. Examples: "A movie has a released event 'Premiere at Cannes Film Festival'.", "A book has a released event 'Book Launch Party'.", "A video game has a released event 'E3 Announcement'."

candidates.label: diseasePreventionInfo
candidates.comment: A disease prevention information relation between a special announcement and a URL or web content providing details about disease prevention. Also called "prevention guidelines", "health advice". Examples: "Special announcement diseasePreventionInfo 'cdc.gov/prevention'", "Public health alert diseasePreventionInfo 'WebContent on handwashing'", "COVID-19 update diseasePreventionInfo 'who.int/prevention'".

candidates.label: legalName
candidates.comment: An official identification relation between an organization and its formally registered name. Also called registered name, official company name, corporate name, full legal name. Examples: An organization has a legalName of 'Acme Corporation Inc.'. A company's legalName is 'Global Solutions LLC'. The charity's legalName is 'Helping Hands Foundation'. Distinct from name, which is the common or display name.

candidates.label: copyrightNotice
candidates.comment: A textual declaration relation between a creative work and the statement describing its copyright aspects. Also called: copyright statement, copyright declaration, copyright text. Examples: "My Novel" copyright notice "© 2023 John Doe", "Company Website" copyright notice "Copyright 2023 Example Corp. All Rights Reserved.", "Academic Paper" copyright notice "Published under CC BY 4.0 license". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which identifies the entity owning the copyright.

candidates.label: newsUpdatesAndGuidelines
candidates.comment: A URL or web content providing news updates and guidelines related to a special announcement. Also called updates page, guidelines link, news and guidance. Examples: "COVID-19 Announcement newsUpdatesAndGuidelines 'https://example.com/covid-updates'", "Emergency Alert newsUpdatesAndGuidelines 'https://gov.example.org/emergency-guidelines'", "Product Recall newsUpdatesAndGuidelines 'https://company.com/recall-info'".

candidates.label: datePublished
candidates.comment: A temporal release relation between a certification or creative work and its date of first publication or broadcast. Also called: publication date, broadcast date, release date. Examples: "Book" date published "1984-06-08", "TV Show Episode" date published "2023-01-01", "Certification" date published "2022-12-01". Distinct from dateCreated, which is the date of creation, and datePosted, which is for online listings.

relations.definition: to have an influence on or impact
relations.embedding_query_text: affects: to have an influence on or impact

chosen_property.label: affects
chosen_property.definition: to have an influence on or impact
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation phrase 'affects'.

candidates.label: affectedBy
candidates.comment: An affected by relation between a medical test and the drugs that can influence its results. Also called influenced by, impacted by, drug interaction. Examples: "A blood test's results are affected by 'anticoagulants'.", "The diagnostic test is affected by 'caffeine'."

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: interactingDrug
candidates.comment: A drug interaction relation between two drugs, where one affects the action or safety of the other. Also called drug-drug interaction, co-administered drug, reactive drug. Examples: Warfarin has an interactingDrug of 'Aspirin'. Antibiotics have an interactingDrug of 'Oral contraceptives'. Statins have an interactingDrug of 'Grapefruit juice'. Distinct from contraindication, which typically refers to a disease or condition that makes a drug unsuitable.

candidates.label: increasesRiskOf
candidates.comment: A risk amplification relation between a medical risk factor and the medical entity (condition, complication) whose likelihood it increases. Also called heightens risk of, raises risk of, predisposes to, contributes to risk of. Examples: Smoking increasesRiskOf lung cancer. High blood pressure increasesRiskOf heart attack. Obesity increasesRiskOf type 2 diabetes.

candidates.label: legislationCommences
candidates.comment: A legislative activation relation between a piece of legislation and another legislation that it brings into legal effect. Also called brings into force, enacts, activates law, sets into effect. Examples: Legislation A legislationCommences 'Legislation B'. The enabling act legislationCommences 'the new regulations'. This decree legislationCommences 'the policy changes'.

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: producer
candidates.comment: A creative role relation between a creative work and the person or organization responsible for its production. Also called production company, executive producer, creator, maker. Examples: A movie has a producer 'Steven Spielberg'. A music album has a producer 'Universal Music Group'. A TV series has a producer 'Shonda Rhimes'. Distinct from director, who is responsible for the creative vision.

candidates.label: assesses
candidates.comment: A relation between a creative work, education event, or learning resource and the competency or learning outcome it is intended to evaluate. Also called: evaluates, measures, tests, gauges. Examples: "LearningResource 'Quiz' assesses 'Understanding of Algebra'", "EducationEvent 'Exam' assesses 'Problem-solving skills'", "CreativeWork 'Rubric' assesses 'Writing proficiency'."

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

relations.definition: to experience or be subjected to a process or change
relations.embedding_query_text: undergoes: to experience or be subjected to a process or change

chosen_property.label: undergoes
chosen_property.definition: to experience or be subjected to a process or change
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation phrase 'undergoes'.

candidates.label: experienceInPlaceOfEducation
candidates.comment: An experience in place of education relation indicating whether a job posting accepts relevant experience as an alternative to formal educational qualifications. Also called: experience substitutes education, education equivalency, alternative qualification. Examples: "Senior Developer Job" experience in place of education "true", "Entry-Level Marketing Position" experience in place of education "false", "Project Manager Role" experience in place of education "true".

candidates.label: experienceRequirements
candidates.comment: An experience requirements relation between a job posting or occupation and the necessary skills and experience for the role. Also called: required experience, skill requirements, professional background. Examples: "Software Engineer Job" experience requirements "5+ years in Java development", "Marketing Manager Occupation" experience requirements "Proven track record in digital marketing campaigns", "Chef Position" experience requirements "Culinary school degree and 3 years restaurant experience".

candidates.label: isInvolvedInBiologicalProcess
candidates.comment: A biological function relation between a biochemical entity and the biological process it participates in. Also called participates in process, role in biological process, contributes to process. Examples: A protein is isInvolvedInBiologicalProcess 'cell division'. An enzyme is isInvolvedInBiologicalProcess 'metabolism'. A hormone is isInvolvedInBiologicalProcess 'growth regulation'.

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: result
candidates.comment: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.

candidates.label: step
candidates.comment: A component relation between a how-to guide and a single instruction, section, or creative work that forms part of the process. Also called "instructional step", "how-to instruction", "process step", "guide step". Examples: "The recipe has step 'Chop vegetables'", "The guide's step is a video tutorial", "This how-to includes a step for assembly.". Distinct from steps, which refers to a collection of steps.

candidates.label: legislationAmends
candidates.comment: A legislative modification relation between a piece of legislation and another legislation that it alters or revises. Also called amends law, modifies legislation, revises act, changes statute. Examples: Legislation A legislationAmends 'Legislation B'. The new act legislationAmends 'the previous statute'. This bill legislationAmends 'the tax code'. Distinct from legislationChanges, which is a broader term for any change, whereas legislationAmends specifically introduces legal changes.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: legislationChanges
candidates.comment: A legislative alteration relation between a piece of legislation and another legislation that it modifies, replaces, corrects, or repeals. Also called alters law, modifies statute, replaces act, repeals legislation. Examples: Legislation X legislationChanges 'Legislation Y'. The new regulation legislationChanges 'several existing laws'. This amendment legislationChanges 'the previous version of the act'. Distinct from legislationAmends, which is a specific type of change (introducing legal changes), and legislationConsolidates, which is about creating a consolidated version.

relations.definition: to contain or comprise as a part
relations.embedding_query_text: includes: to contain or comprise as a part

chosen_property.label: includesObject
chosen_property.justification: The 'includesObject' property from schema.org fits the relation phrase 'includes'.

candidates.label: includesObject
candidates.comment: A composition relation between an offer or product collection and the specific products and their quantities it contains. Also called composed of, contains, comprises, consists of, has as object. Examples: An offer includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 2 apples. A product collection includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 5 books. A demand includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 1 car.

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: includedComposition
candidates.comment: A composition inclusion relation between a music composition and a smaller music composition that is part of it. Also called part of composition, contains composition, movement of. Examples: "A symphony has an included composition as a movement.", "A musical work includes a composition.", "This composition contains several included compositions.". Distinct from hasPart, which is a general part-whole relation for creative works.

candidates.label: hasBioChemEntityPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a biochemical entity and one of its constituent biochemical entities. Also called composed of, contains, includes part, made of. Examples: "A protein has a BioChemEntity part of an amino acid sequence.", "A cell has BioChemEntity parts like organelles.", "A molecule has BioChemEntity parts of atoms."

candidates.label: comprisedOf
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an anatomical system and the anatomical structures or other systems that physically comprise it. Also called "composed of", "consists of", "includes". Examples: "Circulatory system comprisedOf Heart", "Digestive system comprisedOf Stomach".

candidates.label: includedInDataCatalog
candidates.comment: A data catalog inclusion relation between a dataset and the data catalog that contains it. Also called part of catalog, contained in catalog, catalog member. Examples: "A dataset is included in a data catalog.", "The data is part of an included in data catalog.", "This dataset belongs to a specific included in data catalog."

candidates.label: members
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: includes members, comprises, consists of. Examples: "Club Organization members John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership members Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization members Partner Company". Distinct from member, which is a singular form and essentially the same concept.

candidates.label: includedDataCatalog
candidates.comment: A data catalog inclusion relation between a dataset and the data catalog that contains it. Also called part of catalog, contained in catalog, catalog member. Examples: "A dataset is included in a data catalog.", "The data is part of an included data catalog.", "This dataset belongs to a specific included data catalog."

candidates.label: containsSeason
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between a radio, TV, or video game series and a creative work season that is part of it. Also called "includes season", "has season", "season of series". Examples: "TV series 'Friends' containsSeason 'Season 1'", "Video game series 'Halo' containsSeason 'Halo: Combat Evolved'".

candidates.label: containsPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and another smaller place that it contains. Also called "includes place", "encompasses", "holds". Examples: "Country 'France' containsPlace 'Paris'", "City 'Paris' containsPlace 'Eiffel Tower'". Distinct from containedIn or containedInPlace, which are the inverse relations.

relations.definition: to express or declare a fact or opinion
relations.embedding_query_text: states: to express or declare a fact or opinion

chosen_property.label: states
chosen_property.definition: to express or declare a fact or opinion
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation phrase 'states'.

candidates.label: claimInterpreter
candidates.comment: An interpretation relation between a claim and the organization or person who interpreted it from media content. Also called "interpreted by", "claim analyst", "fact-checker". Examples: "News claim claimInterpreter FactCheck.org", "Social media claim claimInterpreter Jane Doe".

candidates.label: printSection
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the specific print section where a news article appeared. Also called section name, newspaper section, print category. Examples: A news article appears in print section 'Sports'. The story is in print section 'Business'. The article's print section is 'Opinion'.

candidates.label: status
candidates.comment: An indication of the current state or status of a medical condition, procedure, or study. Also called "current state", "condition status", "study progress", "procedure status". Examples: "The medical study has status Recruiting", "The patient's condition status is stable", "The procedure's status is completed."

candidates.label: legislationJurisdiction
candidates.comment: A jurisdiction relation between a piece of legislation and the administrative area from which it originates. Also called: originating jurisdiction, legal territory, governing region. Examples: "Federal Law legislationJurisdiction United States", "State Statute legislationJurisdiction California", "EU Directive legislationJurisdiction European Union".

candidates.label: verificationFactCheckingPolicy
candidates.comment: A verification fact-checking policy relation between a news media organization or organization and a disclosure about its verification and fact-checking processes. Also called fact-checking policy, verification standards, editorial policy. Examples: "NewsMediaOrganization verificationFactCheckingPolicy 'https://example.com/fact-check-policy'", "Organization verificationFactCheckingPolicy 'Our journalists verify all claims.'", "News outlet verificationFactCheckingPolicy 'https://example.com/editorial-standards'".

candidates.label: articleSection
candidates.comment: A categorization of an article within a larger publication, such as a magazine or newspaper. Also called: article category, section heading, publication section. Examples: "Article 'Sports News' articleSection 'Sports'", "Article 'Lifestyle Piece' articleSection 'Lifestyle'", "Article 'Editorial' articleSection 'Opinion'."

candidates.label: actionStatus
candidates.comment: An action status relation between an action and its current disposition or state. Also called action state, status of action, disposition. Examples: "A 'purchase' action's action status is 'CompletedActionStatus'.", "A 'shipment' action's action status is 'PotentialActionStatus'."

candidates.label: nationality
candidates.comment: A country representing the nationality of a person. Also called citizenship, country of origin, national identity. Examples: "Person A nationality 'United States'", "Person B nationality 'France'", "Person C nationality 'Japan'". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the location where a person was born.

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim
candidates.comment: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: countryOfOrigin
candidates.comment: A provenance relation between a creative work or product and its country of origin. Also called: origin country, produced in, made in. Examples: "French Wine" country of origin "France", "Japanese Anime" country of origin "Japan", "German Car" country of origin "Germany", "Hollywood Movie" country of origin "United States". Distinct from countryOfAssembly, which specifies where the product was put together.

relations.definition: to separate or detach from a larger organization
relations.embedding_query_text: spun off: to separate or detach from a larger organization

chosen_property.label: spunOff
chosen_property.definition: to separate or detach from a larger organization
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation phrase 'spun off'.

candidates.label: parentOrganization
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between an organization and the larger organization it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is a division of, is a subsidiary of, is part of. Examples: Google is a parent organization of YouTube. A local branch is a parent organization of its national headquarters. A department is a parent organization of its university. Distinct from subOrganization, which points from a larger organization to its smaller components.

candidates.label: subOrganization
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a parent organization and a smaller organization that is a part of it, such as a subsidiary. Also called "subsidiary", "division", "affiliated organization", "part of organization". Examples: "Google has subOrganization YouTube", "The university's subOrganization is the Computer Science Department", "This company owns several subOrganization entities.". Distinct from department, which is a more specific type of sub-organization.

candidates.label: dissolutionDate
candidates.comment: A dissolution date relation between an organization and the date when it was dissolved. Also called "closure date", "ceased operations date", "disbandment date". Examples: "Company 'Acme Corp' dissolutionDate '2023-01-15'", "Non-profit organization dissolutionDate '2022-07-01'", "Partnership dissolutionDate '2024-03-10'".

candidates.label: makesOffer
candidates.comment: An offering relation between an organization or person and the offer for products or services they provide. Also called: offers, provides, sells. Examples: "Retailer makesOffer Discounted Electronics", "Consultant makesOffer Business Strategy Services", "Restaurant makesOffer Dinner Menu".

candidates.label: superEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a smaller event and the larger event of which it is a part. Also called "part of larger event", "parent event", "contained within event", "main event". Examples: "The concert has superEvent the music festival", "The presentation's superEvent is the conference", "This workshop is part of a superEvent summit.". Distinct from subEvent, which points from the larger event to the smaller one.

candidates.label: sourceOrganization
candidates.comment: An affiliation relation between a creative work and the organization on whose behalf its creator was working. Also called "commissioning organization", "producing organization", "organization behind", "publisher organization". Examples: "The research paper's sourceOrganization was MIT", "The documentary's sourceOrganization was BBC", "This report's sourceOrganization is the World Health Organization."

candidates.label: subEvents
candidates.comment: A collection of hierarchical relations between a larger event and multiple smaller events that are components or parts of it. Also called "component events", "nested events", "events within event", "parts of event". Examples: "The conference has subEvents multiple presentations", "The festival's subEvents include several concerts and workshops", "This event comprises many subEvents.". Distinct from subEvent, which refers to a single component event.

candidates.label: subEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.

candidates.label: department
candidates.comment: An organizational structure relation between an organization and one of its departments. Also called: organizational unit, division, branch. Examples: "University" department "Computer Science Department", "Hospital" department "Emergency Room", "Retail Store" department "Pharmacy".

candidates.label: founder
candidates.comment: A founder relation between an organization and the person or organization that established it. Also called: established by, created by, initiated by. Examples: "Microsoft" founder "Bill Gates", "Apple Inc." founder "Steve Jobs", "Google" founder "Larry Page". Distinct from founders, which is specifically for multiple people.

relations.definition: to examine or interpret in detail
relations.embedding_query_text: analyzes: to examine or interpret in detail

chosen_property.label: analyzes
chosen_property.definition: to examine or interpret in detail
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation phrase 'analyzes'.

candidates.label: assesses
candidates.comment: A relation between a creative work, education event, or learning resource and the competency or learning outcome it is intended to evaluate. Also called: evaluates, measures, tests, gauges. Examples: "LearningResource 'Quiz' assesses 'Understanding of Algebra'", "EducationEvent 'Exam' assesses 'Problem-solving skills'", "CreativeWork 'Rubric' assesses 'Writing proficiency'."

candidates.label: claimInterpreter
candidates.comment: An interpretation relation between a claim and the organization or person who interpreted it from media content. Also called "interpreted by", "claim analyst", "fact-checker". Examples: "News claim claimInterpreter FactCheck.org", "Social media claim claimInterpreter Jane Doe".

candidates.label: study
candidates.comment: A relation between a medical entity and a medical study or trial that investigates it. Also called "related study", "investigated by study", "medical trial". Examples: "The drug has study a clinical trial", "The medical condition is part of a study", "This therapy is being evaluated in a study."

candidates.label: studySubject
candidates.comment: An investigative relation between a medical study and the medical entity (condition, therapy, drug, etc.) that is being investigated. Also called "subject of investigation", "research focus", "entity studied", "trial subject". Examples: "The medical study has studySubject a new drug", "The clinical trial's studySubject is a specific medical condition", "This study investigates a studySubject therapy."

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim
candidates.comment: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: measurementTechnique
candidates.comment: A measurement technique relation between a data catalog, data download, dataset, observation, property value, or statistical variable and the technique, method, or technology used for measurement. Also called: measurement approach, data collection method, analytical technique. Examples: "Molecule Concentration Dataset measurementTechnique 'Mass Spectrometry'", "Depression Rating Observation measurementTechnique 'Beck Depression Inventory'", "Water Quality Data measurementTechnique 'Chromatography'". Distinct from measurementMethod, which is a more specific subproperty.

candidates.label: review
candidates.comment: A critical assessment or evaluation of an item, such as a product, service, or creative work. Also called item review, evaluation, critique, assessment. Examples: `Product: Smartphone` review `Customer Review`, `Movie: Inception` review `Film Critic's Review`, `Restaurant: The Fancy Bistro` review `Food Blogger's Review`. Distinct from `reviews`, which is a plural form and often implies a collection.

candidates.label: usedToDiagnose
candidates.comment: A used to diagnose relation between a medical test and a medical condition it is employed to identify. Also called diagnoses, identifies condition, screens for. Examples: "MedicalTest 'MRI' usedToDiagnose 'Brain Tumor'", "MedicalTest 'Blood Test' usedToDiagnose 'Anemia'", "MedicalTest 'X-ray' usedToDiagnose 'Fracture'".

candidates.label: ratingExplanation
candidates.comment: A rating explanation relation between a rating and a brief text providing context or justification for the rating. Also called rating justification, explanation for rating, rating context. Examples: "A product rating includes a rating explanation 'The battery life was excellent, but the camera was disappointing'.", "A fact-check rating has a rating explanation 'The claim was partially true, lacking full context'.", "A service rating has a rating explanation 'The staff were friendly, but wait times were long'."

candidates.label: reviews
candidates.comment: A collection of critical assessments or evaluations pertaining to an item, such as a product, service, or creative work. Also called item reviews, evaluations, critiques, assessments. Examples: `Product: Laptop` reviews `[Review 1, Review 2, ...]`, `Movie: Dune` reviews `[Critic Review, User Review]`, `Restaurant: Pizzeria` reviews `[Google Reviews, Yelp Reviews]`. Distinct from `review`, which typically refers to a single review.

relations.definition: to create or produce something, especially a product or software
relations.embedding_query_text: developed by: to create or produce something, especially a product or software

chosen_property.label: creator
chosen_property.justification: The 'creator' property from schema.org fits the relation phrase 'developed by'.

candidates.label: creator
candidates.comment: An authorship relation between a creative work or user comment and the person or organization responsible for its creation. Also called: author, originator, producer, made by. Examples: "Novel" creator "Jane Doe", "Software" creator "Acme Corp.", "Blog Post" creator "John Smith", "User Review" creator "Anonymous User". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which is about legal ownership.

candidates.label: manufacturer
candidates.comment: A manufacturing relation between a product and the organization that produced it. Also called: produced by, made by, fabricated by. Examples: "Smartphone manufacturer Apple", "Automobile manufacturer Toyota", "Furniture manufacturer IKEA".

candidates.label: productionCompany
candidates.comment: A production relation between a creative work (like a movie or series) and the organization responsible for its creation. Also called produced by, studio, made by, created by. Examples: "The movie 'Dune' was produced by Legendary Pictures.", "The TV series 'The Crown' was produced by Left Bank Pictures.", "The video game 'Cyberpunk 2077' was produced by CD Projekt Red."

candidates.label: produces
candidates.comment: An outcome relation between a service and the tangible thing it generates or provides. Also called generates, yields, creates, provides. Examples: A government service produces a 'passport'. A licensing service produces a 'permit'. A printing service produces 'documents'.

candidates.label: isBasedOn
candidates.comment: A derivation relation between a creative work and the resource (another work, product, or URL) from which it is adapted or modified. Also called derived from, adapted from, based on, inspired by, modification of. Examples: A movie isBasedOn 'a novel'. A software update isBasedOn 'previous version'. A remix isBasedOn 'original song'. Distinct from isBasedOnUrl, which specifically points to a URL as the source.

candidates.label: serviceOutput
candidates.comment: The tangible item or product that is generated or delivered as a result of a service. Also called service product, service deliverable, output of service. Examples: `Passport Application Service` serviceOutput `Passport`, `Permit Application Service` serviceOutput `Building Permit`, `Printing Service` serviceOutput `Printed Documents`.

candidates.label: softwareHelp
candidates.comment: A relation between a software application and a creative work providing assistance or guidance for its use. Also called "application help", "software documentation", "user guide for software". Examples: "Microsoft Word has softwareHelp a user manual", "The app's softwareHelp is an online FAQ", "This softwareHelp explains how to use the program."

candidates.label: softwareVersion
candidates.comment: An identification of the specific version of a software application. Also called "application version", "version number", "software release". Examples: "Firefox has softwareVersion 120.0", "The softwareVersion of the operating system is Windows 11", "This program's softwareVersion is 3.1.4."

candidates.label: targetProduct
candidates.comment: A compatibility relation between software source code and the software application or operating system it is intended for. Also called "compatible with", "designed for", "applies to product", "software target". Examples: "The source code has targetProduct Windows 10", "The script's targetProduct is Microsoft Excel", "This code is written for targetProduct Linux."

candidates.label: material
candidates.comment: A material composition relation between a creative work or product and the material it is made from. Also called: made of, composed of, constructed from. Examples: "Wooden Chair material Wood", "Wool Sweater material Wool", "Paper Book material Paper".

chosen_property.label: owns
chosen_property.justification: The 'owns' property from schema.org fits the relation phrase 'owns'.

candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

candidates.label: owner
candidates.comment: A person or organization that owns a thing. Also called proprietor, possessor, title holder. Examples: "Car owner 'John Doe'", "Company owner 'Acme Corp'", "House owner 'Smith Family Trust'". Distinct from creator, who made the thing.

candidates.label: ownedFrom
candidates.comment: The date and time when ownership of a product was obtained. Also called acquisition date, purchase date, date acquired. Examples: "Car OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2020-01-15'", "House OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2018-06-01T10:00:00'", "Book OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2023-03-10'". Distinct from ownedThrough, which is the date ownership ended.

candidates.label: copyrightHolder
candidates.comment: A legal ownership relation between a creative work and the person or organization holding its copyright. Also called: copyright owner, rights holder, legally owned by. Examples: "The Mona Lisa" copyright holder "The Louvre Museum", "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" copyright holder "J.K. Rowling", "Microsoft Windows" copyright holder "Microsoft Corporation".

candidates.label: ownedThrough
candidates.comment: The date and time when ownership of a product was relinquished. Also called disposal date, date sold, ownership end date. Examples: "Car OwnershipInfo ownedThrough '2023-05-20'", "House OwnershipInfo ownedThrough '2022-11-30T16:00:00'", "Book OwnershipInfo ownedThrough '2024-01-01'". Distinct from ownedFrom, which is the date ownership began.

candidates.label: landlord
candidates.comment: A property ownership relation between a rent action and the person or organization that owns and leases the real estate. Also called property owner, lessor, rental owner, proprietor. Examples: A rent action has a landlord of 'John Doe'. A rent action has a landlord of 'Property Management Inc.'. A lease agreement lists 'Sarah Smith' as the landlord. Distinct from agent, which is the general actor of an action.

candidates.label: numberOfPreviousOwners
candidates.comment: The total number of previous owners of a vehicle, including the current owner. Also called prior owners, owner history count, past owners. Examples: "Used Car A numberOfPreviousOwners 1", "Vintage Vehicle B numberOfPreviousOwners 3", "New Car C numberOfPreviousOwners 0".

candidates.label: ownershipFundingInfo
candidates.comment: Information describing the ownership structure, funding, and grants of an organization, particularly concerning editorial independence for news media. Also called funding transparency, ownership structure, financial backing details. Examples: "News Org A ownershipFundingInfo 'https://news.example.com/about/funding'", "Company B ownershipFundingInfo 'Privately held by XYZ Group.'", "Nonprofit C ownershipFundingInfo 'Funded by grants from various foundations.'". Distinct from funder, which specifically identifies the entity providing funds.

candidates.label: purchaseDate
candidates.comment: A purchase date relation between a product or vehicle and the date it was acquired by its current owner. Also called acquired on, bought on, ownership date. Examples: "A car has a purchase date of 2020-05-10.", "A smartphone has a purchase date of 2023-01-15.", "A house has a purchase date of 2018-07-22.". Distinct from productionDate, which is the date the item was manufactured.

candidates.label: acquiredFrom
candidates.comment: An acquired from relation between ownership information and the organization or person from whom a product was obtained. Also called purchased from, obtained from, source of acquisition. Examples: "The car's ownership info indicates it was acquired from 'Dealership X'.", "The book's ownership info shows it was acquired from 'John Doe'."

chosen_property.label: leads
chosen_property.definition: to be in charge of or direct
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation phrase 'leads'.

candidates.label: advanceBookingRequirement
candidates.comment: An advance booking requirement relation between a demand or offer and the minimum time needed between acceptance and actual usage. Also called lead time, booking lead time, reservation notice. Examples: "A flight offer's advance booking requirement is '24 hours'.", "The concert ticket demand has an advance booking requirement of '7 days'."

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: target
candidates.comment: A destination relation between an action and its intended entry point or URL. Also called "action destination", "target URL", "entry point for action", "leads to". Examples: "The search action has target a search results page", "The button's target is a specific URL", "This action points to a target entry point."

candidates.label: follows
candidates.comment: A follows relation representing a generic uni-directional social connection between two people. Also called: is following, subscribes to, tracks. Examples: "Alice follows Bob", "Charlie follows David", "Eve follows Frank". Distinct from followee, which is the object of a follow action.

candidates.label: directors
candidates.comment: A creative leadership relation between a clip, episode, movie, or video game and the persons who directed it. Also called: directed by, filmmakers, showrunners. Examples: "Movie" directors "Joel Coen, Ethan Coen", "TV Episode" directors "Various Directors", "Video Game" directors "Hideo Kojima, Yoji Shinkawa". Distinct from director, which is a singular property for a single director.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: contributor
candidates.comment: A secondary participation relation for a creative work or event, indicating an organization or person who contributed to it. Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: coach
candidates.comment: A leadership relation between a sports team and the person who acts as its coach. Also called "team coach", "trainer", "manager". Examples: "Basketball team coach John Smith", "Soccer team coach Jane Doe".

candidates.label: previousItem
candidates.comment: A sequential relation between a list item and the list item that immediately precedes it. Also called precedes, comes after, follows. Examples: List item 'B' has a previous item 'A'. The current item's previous item is the one before it. In a breadcrumb trail, the current page has a previous item. Distinct from nextItem, which links to the item that follows.

chosen_property.label: isPartOf
chosen_property.justification: The 'isPartOf' property from schema.org fits the relation phrase 'is part of'.

candidates.label: partOfSystem
candidates.comment: A biological relation between an anatomical structure and the anatomical or organ system it is a component of. Also called is a component of, belongs to, is found in, forms part of. Examples: The heart is part of the circulatory system. The lungs are part of the respiratory system. A bone is part of the skeletal system.

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: partOfSeason
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an episode or clip and the creative work season it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: An episode is part of a season. A clip from a show is part of a season. The season finale is part of a season.

candidates.label: partOfSeries
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an episode, season, or clip and the creative work series it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: An episode is part of a series. A season is part of a series. A clip from a show is part of a series. Distinct from partOfTVSeries, which is specifically for TV series.

candidates.label: partOfTVSeries
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between a TV episode, season, or clip and the TV series it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: A TV episode is part of a TV series. A TV season is part of a TV series. A TV clip is part of a TV series. Distinct from partOfSeries, which is a more general property for any creative work series.

candidates.label: partOfInvoice
candidates.comment: A financial relation between an order and the invoice that includes it for payment. Also called is included in, is billed on, is covered by. Examples: An online purchase order is part of an invoice. A service request order is part of an invoice. Multiple orders can be part of a single invoice.

candidates.label: partOfEpisode
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between a clip and the episode it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is featured in, belongs to, is from. Examples: A highlight reel is part of an episode. A deleted scene is part of an episode. A short preview is part of an episode.

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: partOfOrder
candidates.comment: A logistical relation between a parcel delivery and the larger order it fulfills. Also called fulfills, belongs to, is a shipment for, is included in. Examples: A package delivery is part of an online shopping order. A food delivery is part of a restaurant order. A furniture shipment is part of a home goods order.

chosen_property.label: developsGamesFor
chosen_property.definition: to create games for a particular platform or company
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation phrase 'develops games for'.

candidates.label: game
candidates.comment: A game relation between a game server and the video game that is hosted and played on it. Also called: hosted game, server game, game played. Examples: "Minecraft Server" game "Minecraft", "World of Warcraft Realm" game "World of Warcraft", "CS:GO Server" game "Counter-Strike: Global Offensive".

candidates.label: gamePlatform
candidates.comment: A game platform relation between a video game or series and the electronic systems on which it can be played. Also called: gaming console, supported platform, system compatibility. Examples: "The Last of Us Part II" game platform "PlayStation 4", "Halo Infinite" game platform "Xbox Series X", "Cyberpunk 2077" game platform "PC".

candidates.label: gameEdition
candidates.comment: A game edition relation between a video game and its specific version or release edition. Also called: game version, release edition, special edition. Examples: "Cyberpunk 2077" game edition "Ultimate Edition", "The Witcher 3" game edition "Game of the Year Edition", "Minecraft" game edition "Java Edition".

candidates.label: gameServer
candidates.comment: A game server relation between a video game and the server where it can be played. Also called: hosted on, playable server, game host. Examples: "Minecraft" game server "Hypixel Network", "World of Warcraft" game server "Frostmourne Realm", "Call of Duty" game server "Dedicated Server". Distinct from game, which is the game itself.

candidates.label: gameTip
candidates.comment: A game tip relation between a video game and a creative work providing tips, tactics, or strategies for playing it. Also called: game guide, strategy guide, walkthrough. Examples: "Elden Ring" game tip "Fextralife Wiki", "Chess" game tip "Opening Strategy Guide", "Fortnite" game tip "Building Tactics Video".

candidates.label: gameItem
candidates.comment: A game item relation between a game or video game series and an object within its virtual world that can be collected. Also called: in-game item, collectible, virtual object. Examples: "RPG Game" game item "Health Potion", "Adventure Game" game item "Golden Key", "Strategy Game" game item "Resource Pack".

candidates.label: gameLocation
candidates.comment: A game location relation between a game or video game series and a real or fictional place where the game or part of it is set. Also called: game setting, virtual world, game environment. Examples: "Grand Theft Auto V" game location "Los Santos", "The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild" game location "Hyrule", "Assassin's Creed Valhalla" game location "England".

candidates.label: cheatCode
candidates.comment: A utility relation between a video game or series and a creative work containing cheat codes for it. Also called "game cheats", "unlock codes", "game secrets". Examples: "Video game 'Grand Theft Auto V' cheatCode 'Invincibility code'", "Game series 'The Sims' cheatCode 'Money cheat'".

candidates.label: playMode
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the supported gameplay modes for a video game or series, such as single-player, multi-player, or co-op. Also called game mode, player configuration, gameplay style. Examples: A video game has a play mode of 'SinglePlayer'. A video game has a play mode of 'MultiPlayer'. A video game has a play mode of 'CoOp'.

candidates.label: quest
candidates.comment: A quest relation between a game or video game series and a specific task or mission that players can complete for a reward. Also called mission, task, objective. Examples: "A role-playing game features a quest to 'defeat the dragon'.", "A video game series includes a quest to 'collect all artifacts'.", "An adventure game has a quest to 'rescue the princess'."

chosen_property.label: reportsTo
chosen_property.definition: to be responsible to or answer to someone
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation phrase 'reports to'.

candidates.label: reportNumber
candidates.comment: A report number relation between a report and the unique identifier assigned by its publisher. Also called report ID, document number. Examples: "A financial report has a report number 'FY2023-Q4'.", "A technical report has a report number 'TR-001-2024'.", "A government report has a report number 'GAO-24-123'."

candidates.label: healthcareReportingData
candidates.comment: A healthcare reporting data relation between a hospital and its associated reporting data, such as CDC records or datasets. Also called hospital data, reporting dataset, healthcare metrics. Examples: "A hospital has healthcare reporting data from the CDC.", "The hospital provides healthcare reporting data as a dataset.", "This facility publishes its healthcare reporting data."

candidates.label: diversityStaffingReport
candidates.comment: A diversity staffing report relation between an organization (e.g., news media) and an article or URL containing a report on staffing diversity issues. Also called "staff diversity report", "workforce diversity data", "inclusion metrics report". Examples: "News media organization diversityStaffingReport 'Article on newsroom diversity'", "Company diversityStaffingReport 'URL to annual diversity report'", "Organization diversityStaffingReport 'Self-reported staffing data'".

candidates.label: knownVehicleDamages
candidates.comment: A vehicle condition relation between a vehicle and a textual description of its known damages, whether repaired or not. Also called vehicle damage report, damage history, known defects, condition notes. Examples: A used car has knownVehicleDamages 'minor dent on rear bumper'. A vehicle has knownVehicleDamages 'repaired fender bender'. A truck has knownVehicleDamages 'scratches on passenger side door'. Distinct from vehicleCondition, which is a general assessment, not specific damages.

candidates.label: employmentUnit
candidates.comment: An employment unit relation between a job posting and the organization (department, unit, or facility) where the job is performed. Also called "department", "work unit", "reporting unit". Examples: "Job posting 'Software Engineer' employmentUnit 'Engineering Department'", "Job 'Sales Associate' employmentUnit 'Retail Store #123'", "Job 'HR Specialist' employmentUnit 'Human Resources Division'".

candidates.label: coverageStartTime
candidates.comment: A temporal boundary relation between a live blog posting and the time when its event coverage begins. Also called: coverage start, reporting start time, live blog commencement. Examples: "Election Night Live Blog" coverage start time "2024-11-05T18:00:00Z", "Sports Event Live Update" coverage start time "2023-07-15T14:00:00Z", "Conference Live Blog" coverage start time "2023-10-27T09:00:00Z". Distinct from coverageEndTime, which indicates when coverage concludes.

candidates.label: associatedArticle
candidates.comment: A news article linked to a media object. Also called: related article, accompanying article, news story link. Examples: "MediaObject 'Video of Protest' associatedArticle 'NewsArticle on Protest'", "MediaObject 'Photo of Event' associatedArticle 'Article about Event'."

candidates.label: associatedMediaReview
candidates.comment: A media review related to another review by common content, topic, or claim. Also called: related media review, linked media assessment. Examples: "Review 'ClaimReview of Statement' associatedMediaReview 'MediaReview of Article'", "Review 'ProductReview' associatedMediaReview 'VideoReview'". Distinct from associatedClaimReview, which links to a claim review.

candidates.label: reviewedBy
candidates.comment: The person or organization responsible for reviewing the content of a webpage for accuracy or completeness. Also called content reviewer, page editor, accuracy checker. Examples: `Medical Information Page` reviewedBy `Dr. Jane Doe`, `News Article` reviewedBy `Fact-Checking Organization`, `Research Paper` reviewedBy `Peer Review Board`. Distinct from `author`, which indicates who created the content, not who reviewed it.

candidates.label: associatedClaimReview
candidates.comment: A claim review related to another review by common content, topic, or claim. Also called: related claim review, linked claim assessment. Examples: "Review 'MediaReview of Article' associatedClaimReview 'ClaimReview of Statement'", "Review 'FactCheck' associatedClaimReview 'Another FactCheck'". Distinct from associatedMediaReview, which links to a media review.
